signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: The G10 scorecard confirms JPY as the weekly leader up +0.911% across 7 pairs against CHF as the primary laggard down −0.733% across 6 pairs, generating a wide 1.644% spread. Multiple high-impact geopolitical headlines detail Strait of Hormuz maritime security tensions and warning shots, driving safe-haven asset divergence. Spot CHF/JPY trades at 189.084, down −0.38% intraday, while the cross carry favors JPY via SNB 0.00% vs BoJ 1.25% with a −125bp deficit. Furthermore, BEER valuation flags CHF/JPY as structurally cheap at z=−1.96σ relative to fair value. The combination of dominant JPY scorecard outperformance, geopolitical risk premium, and negative CHF carry reinforces relative CHF underperformance against JPY. Trade bias: Bearish CHF/JPY; bilateral divergence supported by JPY outperformance and negative carry. Catalyst: Japan retail sales and industrial production at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Strait of Hormuz de-escalation leads to broad JPY carry-trade resumption.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Vol Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.37, positioned above the SMA20 at 156.40 but capped below the SMA50 at 158.60 and SMA200 at 158.45. Options pricing reflects an extreme downside bias, with 25d risk reversals printing at −2.57, indicating aggressive demand for downside put protection. This sharp put skew unfolds while ATM IV at 9.1% sits below HV30 at 10.2%, creating a negative vol risk premium of −1.1%. Cross-asset context shows MOVE at the 96th percentile of its trailing year versus VIX at the 27th percentile, signaling substantial rate volatility not yet priced into equities. Although the Fed-BoJ policy differential stands at Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% with a +275bp USD carry advantage, options traders are actively hedging downside exposure rather than chasing spot gains. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish USD/JPY; heavy options put skew constrains upside progress despite carry support. Catalyst: Japan retail sales and industrial production at 23:50 UTC. Risk: A daily close above the SMA50/SMA200 cluster at 158.60 invalidates the options downside hedging structure.

signals.title: AUD/USD — CB Differential + Technical Levels
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7020, testing major structural support directly at its SMA200 of 0.7026 while remaining below its SMA20 at 0.7141 and SMA50 at 0.7096. Central bank policy spreads favor the Australian dollar, with RBA at 4.35% (on hold) vs Fed at 4.00% (hiking), generating a −35bp AUD carry premium. Positioning data reveals Leveraged Funds hold net long +55,684 contracts (pctl 81, z +0.92), though net long additions fell by −3,615 contracts WoW. Market pricing anticipates an RBA rate hike decision at 04:30 UTC, providing an imminent policy catalyst. A sustained technical failure below the SMA200 would threaten the long-term bullish trend despite policy rate support. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; policy carry premium supports defense of major moving average support. Catalyst: RBA interest rate decision at 04:30 UTC. Risk: RBA leaves rates unchanged and strikes a dovish tone, forcing an SMA200 breakdown.
evidence: RBA 4.35% vs Fed 4.00% — -35bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: EUR/USD — Rates Driver + Technical Levels
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1374, locked in a downtrend below its SMA20 at 1.1539, SMA50 at 1.1538, and SMA200 at 1.1625. US 5Y yields rose +25bp over 5D (FRED, as of Sep 24), driven entirely by real rates with real +24bp and breakeven +1bp, creating a real-yield-led dollar bid. Policy rates firmly favor the greenback, with Fed at 4.00% (hiking) vs ECB at 2.65% (hiking), delivering a +135bp spread in favor of USD. Meanwhile, CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net short −58,805 contracts (pctl 19, z −1.01), adding −7,450 contracts short WoW as institutional sellers press downside momentum. With spot trading well beneath all major daily moving averages, rate dynamics continue to anchor the pair lower. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent real-yield expansion and policy carry favor dollar strength. Catalyst: Germany and France CPI releases at 06:45 UTC and 12:00 UTC. Risk: Higher-than-forecast European inflation prints prompt aggressive ECB terminal rate repricing.
evidence: Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% — +135bp carry favors USD
